0.body: Bazel rules for Terraform and OpenTofu . Every terraform_* rule has a tofu_* twin that takes the same inputs and runs the other engine; the text below says terraform and means both.
0.title: rules_terraform

1.body:
bazel_dep(name = "rules_terraform", version = "{version}") Toolchains for both engines are registered by rules_terraform's own MODULE.bazel. A build uses one release per engine: the root module's toolchain tag, else the newest shipped in //terraform/private:versions.bzl / //tofu/private:versions.bzl , which carry the three newest releases with their checksums. terraform = use_extension("@rules_terraform//terraform:extensions.bzl", "terraform")
terraform.toolchain(version = "1.9.8") tofu = use_extension("@rules_terraform//tofu:extensions.bzl", "tofu")
tofu.toolchain(version = "1.9.1") Any release works there. One outside the shipped table costs a single fetch of its SHA256SUMS, recorded as a fact in MODULE.bazel.lock. Changing the release is editing the tag; a tag in a dependency is ignored. Nothing has to be installed on the host: the engine, provider archives and modules are all fetched by Bazel, and every bazel run and bazel test below uses the toolchain engine.
1.title: Setup

10.body:
One tag declares both halves of a root's external dependencies, because that is how the engine treats them: init installs the providers the lock pins and the modules the module blocks name in one step. terraform = use_extension("@rules_terraform//terraform:extensions.bzl", "terraform")
terraform.deps( name = "my_deps", lock = "//path/to:.terraform.lock.hcl", # optional: providers roots = ["//path/to:main.tf"], # optional: registry and git modules named in that directory # registry = "registry.opentofu.org", # default follows the extension
)
use_repo(terraform, "my_deps") @my_deps carries every provider in the lock, the lock itself, and every external module the roots name; a terraform_module that depends on it needs no lock attribute, and a maintainer who adds a provider edits required_providers and reruns the lock updater with no BUILD change. @my_deps//:providers, @my_deps//:modules and @my_deps//<namespace>_<name> are the parts. Archives are pooled across hubs, so two locks that agree on a version fetch it once, and only the platform a build resolves is fetched. The attributes are on the extension page .
10.title: The deps tag

11.body: The lock is Terraform's own .terraform.lock.hcl. The terraform_providers_lock updater writes it by running the toolchain engine's providers lock -platform=<all> over the sources, which is the one path that records h1: hashes for every platform at once; the engine's own init locks the platform it runs on only. The default set is linux_amd64, linux_arm64, darwin_amd64, darwin_arm64 and windows_amd64. The extension asks the registry only where each archive lives; the archive's checksum must be one of the lock's zh: hashes, so the registry cannot change what is installed. A platform is left out of a hub only when the registry says the version was never published for it; every other failed lookup fails the evaluation, so an outage cannot leave a platform permanently missing from the lockfile. The build installs each provider under .terraform/providers/<registry>/<namespace>/<name>/<version>/<platform>/ and rewrites the h1: hashes in the tree's copy of the lock to the installed files, which is what lets the engine accept them.
11.title: Providers

12.breadcrumbs: Introduction » Providers built in the repo
12.title: Providers built in the repo

13.body:
A module block whose source is a registry address is resolved when the extension evaluates: the highest version satisfying the block's constraint is chosen once and recorded as a fact in MODULE.bazel.lock, and every later evaluation declares it until an upgrade is asked for. List the directory in a deps tag's roots; every .tf file in it is scanned, and modules composed of other registry or git modules are followed. terraform.deps( name = "shared", lock = "//:.terraform.lock.hcl", roots = [ "//envs/prod/app:main.tf", "//modules/naming:main.tf", # a library whose blocks name a registry module ],
) Archives come straight from GitHub, which is where the public registries host their modules; a registry module hosted elsewhere is an error with the address, and is supplied by hand as below. A source written with its own hostname (app.terraform.io/acme/vpc/aws) is resolved against that host. OpenTofu users use the tofu extension's deps tag, which defaults to registry.opentofu.org.
13.title: Registry modules

14.body:
A module block whose source is a git address goes through the same roots scan with no registry involved, in the three spellings Terraform accepts: git::https://… or git::ssh://…, the scp-like git@host:org/repo.git, and the github.com/org/repo shorthand, each with an optional //subdir and ?ref=. module "vpc" { source = "git::ssh://git@git.example.com/acme/terraform-modules.git//vpc?ref=v1.4.0"
} What the ref pins. A commit id is exact. A tag is looked up once and what it names is recorded, so a moved tag is not followed. A branch, or no ?ref= meaning the default branch, is resolved to a commit the first time and recorded the same way: a choice, like a version constraint, that only RULES_TERRAFORM_UPGRADE moves. The native CLI follows such a source live on every init, so a tag or commit in the block is what keeps the two workflows on one revision. GitHub over https needs no git: the extension fetches the archive GitHub serves for the ref, records its integrity, and declares an http_archive pinned by it. Every other remote , ssh:// to GitHub included, goes through the host's git: the ref is resolved with ls-remote, checked out once to record the commit and read the module's own references, and built as a new_git_repository of that commit, fetched with the host's credentials. git has to be on PATH when the extension evaluates and when the repository is fetched. Not handled: ?sshkey=, submodules, and non-git sources such as plain https:// archives or s3::.
14.title: Git modules

15.body:
Fetch the archive with any repository rule, declare a terraform_external_module in its build file with source copied verbatim from the module block, and put the target in deps; the build installs it under every block whose source matches. # MODULE.bazel
http_archive = use_repo_rule("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")
http_archive( name = "acme_vpc", urls = ["https://git.example.com/acme/terraform-vpc/-/archive/v1.4.0/terraform-vpc-v1.4.0.tar.gz"], strip_prefix = "terraform-vpc-v1.4.0", integrity = "sha256-…", build_file_content = """
load("@rules_terraform//terraform:defs.bzl", "terraform_external_module")
terraform_external_module( name = "module", source = "https://git.example.com/acme/terraform-vpc/-/archive/v1.4.0/terraform-vpc-v1.4.0.tar.gz", srcs = glob(["**/*.tf"]), visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)
""",
)

15.title: Modules the extension cannot fetch

16.title: Local modules

17.body:
The extensions are reproducible = True: given the same tags, files and facts they declare the same repositories. Every answer taken from the network is a fact in MODULE.bazel.lock: a tagged engine release's checksums, where a provider archive lives, the version a module constraint resolved to, the commit a git ref named, an archive's integrity. A .tf edit under a roots directory re-evaluates the extension, but with warm facts that makes no network calls. Facts persist only while the lockfile is enabled, so downstream: common --lockfile_mode=update
# or, once confident:
common --lockfile_mode=strict and commit MODULE.bazel.lock. That gives deterministic module versions however loosely the constraints are written, and a PR-visible diff whenever a resolution changes. --lockfile_mode=off resolves live on every evaluation, exactly as terraform init does. An exact pin in a module block is still worth writing: it is the only form the native init also treats as fixed.
17.title: Reproducibility

18.body: A recorded resolution is kept on purpose. To move a constraint or a branch to what it resolves to today: RULES_TERRAFORM_UPGRADE=1 bazel fetch //... # or --repo_env=RULES_TERRAFORM_UPGRADE=1 Every constraint and git ref is resolved again and the facts rewritten; facts that are properties of a published version, such as an archive's integrity, are kept. Review the MODULE.bazel.lock diff and commit it. Editing a block's source, version or ?ref= is itself a new key, so a changed block resolves on the next bazel fetch without the switch.
18.title: Upgrading

20.body: terraform_binary — bazel run wrapper for any terraform subcommand. terraform_module — declares a .tf module with providers and deps. terraform_external_module — supplies a module fetched from outside the workspace (git, private hosts) to deps. terraform_provider — declares a provider built in the repo. Registry providers come from a deps tag's hub instead. terraform_test — runs Terraform's HCL native test framework, reporting each run block as a JUnit test case. terraform_plan_test — runs a real plan and keeps it as a reviewable test output; needs network. terraform_validate_test / aspect — terraform validate as a Bazel test/aspect. terraform_fmt_test / aspect — terraform fmt -check as a Bazel test/aspect. terraform_providers_lock — bazel run updater that writes .terraform.lock.hcl with the toolchain engine; nothing needs installing on the host. terraform_providers_lock_test — fails when the lock file and the required_providers blocks disagree.

23.body: load("@rules_terraform//terraform:terraform_binary.bzl", "terraform_binary") terraform_binary(name, env, root, workspace) Runs terraform on a terraform_module root. Arguments pass through: bazel run //x:terraform -- plan, -- apply, -- state list. The engine runs in a temp copy of the built module directory, providers and modules already installed, so nothing is fetched at run time. init is the exception: it installs that directory into the module's source directory and initializes the backend there, so the native CLI works in that directory afterwards. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required env Environment variables for the engine, set over the host's for a run and over the hermetic one for a test: TF_VAR_<name> for a root keyed on an input variable, TF_LOG, TF_CLI_ARGS_plan. Values are literal. TF_WORKSPACE here and workspace must agree. Dictionary: String -> String optional {} root The terraform_module target that serves as the root module. Label required workspace Run in this Terraform workspace, over anything the environment or --test_env sets. Unset, the environment's TF_WORKSPACE applies, else default. One test per workspace is how a root keyed on terraform.workspace gets each one checked, and one binary per workspace runs it with no workspace select first. String optional ""
23.title: terraform_binary

The deps tag declares one per registry or git module it resolves. Declare one yourself, in the build_file_content of an http_archive or git_repository, for a module the extension cannot fetch. source must match the module block verbatim; list the target in the consuming terraform_module's deps. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required srcs Every file of the module's repository or archive, not only the module's own: templates and other data the configuration reads, and the siblings a ../ source inside it names. List of labels optional [] source The source string exactly as the module blocks write it. The module is installed under every block whose source matches. String required subdir The module's directory inside srcs: the //subdir of the source, empty for the archive root. String optional "" version The module's version, for a registry module. Leave it empty for a git or other source: the manifest only accepts a semantic version. String optional ""

31.body: load("@rules_terraform//terraform:terraform_module.bzl", "terraform_module") terraform_module(name, deps, srcs, data, disposable_state, lock) One directory of terraform configuration: a root module, or a child that another module's module block names. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required deps What the configuration references: child terraform_modules for its local module blocks, a dependency hub (@<name> from a deps tag, or its //:providers / //:modules halves) or single @<name>//<namespace>_<name> providers, and terraform_provider or terraform_external_module targets. The module block names a child's path; deps says which target supplies it. A child in a package under this one lands at its relative path; any other is matched to the block whose source ends with its package name. List of labels optional [] srcs The configuration files of this module: .tf, .tf.json, all directly in this target's package. A nested directory of configuration is its own module target, named by a module block. List of labels optional [] data Additional files or targets that should be available at runtime. List of labels optional [] disposable_state Whether local state may go with the run, for a module with no backend or cloud block. True, the default: the engine keeps state in the run's temp directory, which is deleted afterwards; a run that wrote state is kept and its path printed. False: state is kept under bazel-out/rules_terraform/ across runs, until bazel clean. An error when the module declares a backend. Boolean optional True lock The module's .terraform.lock.hcl. Not needed when deps names a dependency hub, which carries its lock. Label optional None

Needs the network. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required output Where to write the lock, relative to this package: .terraform.lock.hcl. String required platforms Platforms to record hashes for, as linux_amd64. Default: linux_amd64, linux_arm64, darwin_amd64, darwin_arm64, windows_amd64. 37.body: load("@rules_terraform//terraform:terraform_providers_lock_test.bzl", "terraform_providers_lock_test") terraform_providers_lock_test(name, lock, target) Fails when .terraform.lock.hcl does not match what the module tree requires: every module the init aspect placed, root, local children and installed external ones, and in each the providers required_providers declares plus the ones resource, data, ephemeral and provider blocks imply. A provider the configuration needs but the lock lacks fails, and so does a lock entry nothing needs. Network-free; no engine runs. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required lock The .terraform.lock.hcl file being verified. Label required target The terraform_module whose module tree is being checked. Label required
37.title: terraform_providers_lock_test

4.body:
bazel run //path/to:terraform -- plan
bazel run //path/to:terraform -- apply The binary copies the module directory the build assembled, .tf files, local child modules at their source paths, the lock and a populated .terraform/, into a temp dir and runs the engine there with the arguments given. The temp dir is removed when the command finishes. Relative file arguments (-out=tfplan, -var-file=x.tfvars) resolve against it, so pass absolute paths. Because the build already installed the providers and the module manifest, the only thing a run-time init still contributes is backend setup, so the binary runs one only before subcommands that need a backend. version, fmt, validate, test and metadata skip it and work offline against a module with a remote backend. State. A module with a backend or cloud block is unaffected: its state belongs to the backend. A module with neither keeps state where the native CLI keeps it, the working directory, which here is the temp dir, so by default state goes with the run: disposable_state on the terraform_module is True. A run that did write state is kept and its path printed, so the record of an apply never vanishes silently, but the next run starts fresh. Where state must outlive the run with no backend (bootstrapping the bucket that will hold real state, a sandbox kept for days), set disposable_state = False: the local backend is pointed at a per-module directory under bazel-out/rules_terraform/, which bazel clean deletes and which is named after every state-writing command. Setting it on a module that declares a backend is an error. Environment. bazel run keeps the operator's environment, which is where credential helpers and TF_WORKSPACE live. The tests and the validate aspect run the engine with the CLI configuration disabled (TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE pointed at an empty file, CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1, TF_IN_AUTOMATION=1), so a ~/.terraformrc on one machine cannot change what a check reports.
4.title: terraform_binary

47.body:
The extension always materializes one hub repo (@terraform_toolchains) that declares a toolchain per platform for one Terraform release, and @terraform, the CLI hub. rules_terraform's own MODULE.bazel use_repos the toolchain hub and register_toolchainss it, so downstream users get toolchain resolution for free. Per-platform http_archives are lazy; only the resolved platform is fetched. The release is the root module's toolchain tag, else the newest shipped in //terraform/private:versions.bzl (the three newest when the table was generated carry checksums). For any other release the extension fetches its SHA256SUMS once and records the checksums as facts in MODULE.bazel.lock. # Nothing to do beyond `bazel_dep` to use the newest shipped release.
bazel_dep(name = "rules_terraform", version = "...") # To use another release:
terraform = use_extension("@rules_terraform//terraform:extensions.bzl", "terraform")
terraform.toolchain(version = "1.9.8") terraform.toolchain Attribute Type Description version string (required) The release, e.g. 1.9.8. Root module only, at most one tag; tags in dependencies are ignored. A build has one engine release, and changing it is editing the tag.
47.title: terraform.toolchain

48.title: terraform.deps

49.body: Everything under //tofu mirrors //terraform but binds to //tofu:toolchain_type. Rule bodies are identical — only the resolved toolchain differs — so behavior stays in lockstep between the two engines. Data-only rules (tofu_module, tofu_external_module, tofu_provider, tofu_provider_group) are literal aliases for their terraform_* counterparts, provided so an OpenTofu-only project never has to import a terraform_* symbol.
49.title: OpenTofu Rules

5.body:
bazel run //path/to:terraform -- init is the one subcommand that does not run in the temp dir, where its work would be deleted with it. It installs what the build constructed into the module's source directory, so the native CLI works there afterwards. bazel run //envs/prod/app:terraform -- init
cd envs/prod/app
terraform plan # native CLI, providers and modules from the build The directory is the root module's package under the checkout, wherever the command was run from; BUILD_WORKSPACE_DIRECTORY and the target decide it, not the shell's cwd (that is the @terraform hub's job). The runner: copies the built .terraform/providers/ and .terraform/modules/ over whatever is there, keeping .terraform/environment and the saved backend configuration, as a native re-init keeps them; writes .terraform.lock.hcl next to the sources only when the module has none of its own (it depends on a shared hub), and says so; adds the host platform's h1: hash to the lock for any installed provider the lock lacks it for, one line each, and says so. An unpacked package can only be verified by its h1:, so a lock made on another platform, or natively with fewer -platforms than the updater records, would make the engine refuse the package it is standing next to. It is the line providers lock -platform=<host> would add; commit it, or regenerate the lock for every platform with the updater; runs the engine's init -get=false -plugin-dir=.terraform/providers in that directory with the remaining arguments appended, which is where the backend gets configured. Each init flag is either the backend's business, which passes through, or the build's, which is refused with the Bazel path named: Flag Under the binary Why -backend-config=…, -backend=false passes through Backend configuration is the module's, not the build's. -reconfigure passes through Re-reads the backend block, ignoring the saved configuration. The staged runs are implicitly always reconfigured, since a fresh copy has none saved; in place it matters. -migrate-state, -force-copy pass through Moves state from the previously saved backend configuration to the current one. It needs that saved configuration, which only a persisted directory has, so this is the only place under Bazel it can work. -input, -lock, -lock-timeout, -no-color, -json pass through Plain engine options. -lockfile=readonly passes through Forbids every lock write, step 3 included: a lock without the host's hash is then an error naming the updater rather than an edit. -upgrade refused Would re-resolve providers against the plugin dir and rewrite the lock. The versions are facts of the build: bazel run //path/to:providers_lock.update for providers, RULES_TERRAFORM_UPGRADE=1 bazel fetch for modules (see Upgrading ). -get refused The build installs the modules; the manifest is theirs. -plugin-dir refused The build's providers are the plugin directory. -from-module refused A root module is a terraform_module target. -chdir (global) refused The target names the module directory. -help passes through Answered by the engine, with nothing installed. .terraform/ is the engine's cache and belongs in .gitignore; Gazelle and the rules ignore it, and a Bazel run never reads it. This is the one bazel run that writes into the source tree, and only because it was asked to. The next bazel run //path/to:terraform -- plan still starts from a fresh copy.
5.title: Initializing in place

6.body: The rules add no workspace concept of their own; they use Terraform's. TF_WORKSPACE in the environment selects one for every project in a run: --action_env=TF_WORKSPACE=prod for the validate aspect, --test_env=TF_WORKSPACE=prod for the test rules, the shell for bazel run. A root whose configuration is keyed on terraform.workspace gets each of its workspaces checked by one test target per workspace, with the workspace attribute of terraform_validate_test, terraform_test or terraform_plan_test forcing it, and no_validate on the module where the default workspace is not a valid one. A workspace select inside a bazel run changes only the temp copy, so it does not carry to the next run and the runner says so; workspace new still creates the workspace in the backend.
6.title: Workspaces

Needs the network. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required output Where to write the lock, relative to this package: .terraform.lock.hcl. String required platforms Platforms to record hashes for, as linux_amd64. Default: linux_amd64, linux_arm64, darwin_amd64, darwin_arm64, windows_amd64. List of strings optional [] target The terraform_module the lock covers, its local child modules included. Label required

A provider the configuration needs but the lock lacks fails, and so does a lock entry nothing needs. Network-free; no engine runs. 65.body: load("@rules_terraform//tofu:tofu_module.bzl", "tofu_module") tofu_module(name, deps, srcs, data, disposable_state, lock) One directory of tofu configuration: a root module, or a child that another module's module block names. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required deps What the configuration references: child terraform_modules for its local module blocks, a dependency hub (@<name> from a deps tag, or its //:providers / //:modules halves) or single @<name>//<namespace>_<name> providers, and terraform_provider or terraform_external_module targets. The module block names a child's path; deps says which target supplies it. A child in a package under this one lands at its relative path; any other is matched to the block whose source ends with its package name. List of labels optional [] srcs The configuration files of this module: .tf, .tf.json, .tofu, .tofu.json, all directly in this target's package. A nested directory of configuration is its own module target, named by a module block. List of labels optional [] data Additional files or targets that should be available at runtime. List of labels optional [] disposable_state Whether local state may go with the run, for a module with no backend or cloud block. True, the default: the engine keeps state in the run's temp directory, which is deleted afterwards; a run that wrote state is kept and its path printed. False: state is kept under bazel-out/rules_terraform/ across runs, until bazel clean. An error when the module declares a backend. Boolean optional True lock The module's .terraform.lock.hcl. Not needed when deps names a dependency hub, which carries its lock. Label optional None

7.body: terraform_validate_test and terraform_fmt_test are validate and fmt -check as Bazel tests. The same checks exist as aspects, which the examples' .bazelrc attaches so bazel build //... runs them over every module without a target per module; no_validate and no_format tags opt a module out. terraform_test runs the engine's native test framework. Each run block is reported as a JUnit test case through XML_OUTPUT_FILE, so bazel test summaries show which run failed. Terraform writes the report itself with -junit-xml; for OpenTofu the runner builds it from the -json-into event stream and keeps that stream too. terraform_plan_test runs a real plan and keeps plan.tfplan, plan.json and plan.txt as undeclared outputs under bazel-testlogs/<pkg>/<name>/test.outputs/, so a plan can be reviewed from CI artefacts. It passes when the plan succeeds, or with expect_no_changes only when the plan is empty. A plan reaches the backend and the provider APIs, so the target is tagged requires-network and credentials go through --test_env; providers that work offline (null, local, random) need neither. Plans hold sensitive values, so treat the artefacts as you would the state. terraform_providers_lock_test fails when .terraform.lock.hcl does not cover what the module tree requires: every provider a required_providers block declares or a resource, data, ephemeral or provider block implies, in the root and in every installed module. No network, no engine.
7.title: Tests and review artefacts

Each run block is a JUnit test case in Bazel's XML report, and the lock and module manifest the test ran against are kept as undeclared test outputs. --test_arg is ignored. Name required env Environment variables for the engine, set over the host's for a run and over the hermetic one for a test: TF_VAR_<name> for a root keyed on an input variable, TF_LOG, TF_CLI_ARGS_plan. Values are literal. TF_WORKSPACE here and workspace must agree. Dictionary: String -> String optional {} env_inherit Variables the test takes from the environment bazel test ran in, AWS_PROFILE say. The variables tests scrub for hermeticity (the CLI configuration ones) cannot be inherited, and the runner says so. List of strings optional [] root The terraform_module target that serves as the root module. Label required workspace Run in this Terraform workspace, over anything the environment or --test_env sets. Unset, the environment's TF_WORKSPACE applies, else default. One test per workspace is how a root keyed on terraform.workspace gets each one checked, and one binary per workspace runs it with no workspace select first. String optional ""

76.body: One module extension lives in //tofu:extensions.bzl, tofu, with the same two tag classes as the terraform extension.
76.title: OpenTofu Extensions

77.body:
The extension always materializes @tofu_toolchains, a hub declaring a toolchain per platform for one OpenTofu release, the root module's toolchain tag or else the newest shipped in //tofu/private:versions.bzl, and @tofu, the CLI hub. rules_terraform's own MODULE.bazel registers the hub so downstream users get toolchain resolution for free. # Nothing to do beyond `bazel_dep` to use the newest shipped release.
bazel_dep(name = "rules_terraform", version = "...") # To use another release:
tofu = use_extension("@rules_terraform//tofu:extensions.bzl", "tofu")
tofu.toolchain(version = "1.9.1") tofu.toolchain takes the same version attribute as the Terraform extension's tag, with the same root-only rule; see the Terraform page . For a tagged release the extension fetches that release's SHA256SUMS once and records the checksums as facts in MODULE.bazel.lock.
77.title: tofu.toolchain

78.body:
The same deps tag class as the terraform extension, defaulting to registry.opentofu.org. An OpenTofu-only repository uses it for everything and never loads //terraform:extensions.bzl: tofu = use_extension("@rules_terraform//tofu:extensions.bzl", "tofu")
tofu.deps( name = "app", lock = "//path/to/module:.terraform.lock.hcl", # written by tofu roots = ["//path/to/module:main.tf"],
)
use_repo(tofu, "app") The attributes are those documented for the terraform extension ; only the default registry differs. That default matters: registry.opentofu.org serves OpenTofu's own builds of the hashicorp/* providers, whose archive hashes differ from HashiCorp's, so a lock file written by tofu has to be resolved against it. Write the lock with the module's tofu_providers_lock updater and it will be. Each extension pools its own archives. A repository using both engines against the same dependencies should declare them through one extension rather than both, or the same archive is fetched twice.
78.title: tofu.deps

79.body: rules_terraform ships a Gazelle language per engine. It writes the BUILD files the rules need from the configuration itself: one module target per directory of .tf files, with deps kept in step with the module blocks, and the binary and lock targets for a root.
79.title: Gazelle

8.body:
Two repositories let you invoke the toolchain engine in whatever directory you are standing in, like the native CLI: cd path/to/my/tf/module
bazel run @terraform -- providers lock
bazel run @tofu -- state list The wrapper chdirs to $BUILD_WORKING_DIRECTORY before exec-ing the engine. It does no init aspect and no .terraform/ construction: a terraform init there runs against the source tree and hits the network. Reach for it for one-off CLI invocations against a directory with no terraform_binary. Downstream, bind the names: terraform = use_extension("@rules_terraform//terraform:extensions.bzl", "terraform")
use_repo(terraform, "terraform") bazel run @rules_terraform//terraform:format (or //tofu:format) rewrites the .tf files of every module in the workspace with the toolchain engine's fmt; pass target patterns to narrow it.
8.title: The @terraform and @tofu hubs

80.title: Setup

81.body: The directory Generated has configuration files terraform_module(name = <directory name>, srcs = [...], data = [...], deps = [...]) also declares a backend or cloud block plus terraform_binary(name = "terraform") and terraform_providers_lock(name = "providers_lock.update") also has a .terraform.lock.hcl plus terraform_providers_lock_test(name = "providers_lock"), and the updater if the directory is not a root holds .tofu files the tofu_* kinds instead srcs are the files the engine loads, .tf and .tf.json, plus .tofu and .tofu.json under OpenTofu. data is everything else a native run in that directory could read: the remaining files, and the contents of subdirectories that are not packages of their own. Build files, the lock, state, and dotfiles are left out, as is anything under .terraform/. deps has two parts. Every module block with a local source (./… or ../…) resolves to the module target in that directory; a directory nothing generates a target for is reported. Then the dependency hubs: the ones a tf_deps_hub directive names, or, for a root with a lock file and no directive, @tf_<path> with / and - replaced by _. Rules are merged, not overwritten: a hand-written tags, visibility, or disposable_state stays, comments stay, and an attribute written as a glob() is left alone with a warning, since a list cannot be merged into it. Delete the glob to let Gazelle write the list.
81.title: What a directory becomes

82.body: Directive Meaning # gazelle:tf_engine terraform|tofu Which engine's rules a directory tree gets. Unset, a directory with .tofu files is OpenTofu's, the rest Terraform's. # gazelle:tf_kind root|module|auto Force a root (binary and lock targets) or a library. auto, the default, reads the configuration for a backend. # gazelle:tf_deps_hub NAME... The hubs (@NAME) modules under the directory depend on. An empty value clears an inherited one. # gazelle:tf_default_visibility LABEL... Visibility written on new library modules under the directory. An existing rule keeps its own. Directives inherit down the tree, so one tf_deps_hub on a module library's parent directory covers every module in it, and one tf_engine tofu at the repository root makes an OpenTofu-only repository.
82.title: Directives

83.body: It does not write .terraform.lock.hcl; that is providers_lock.update. It does not declare the deps tags in MODULE.bazel; the hub names it writes are the names those tags must have. And it does not read expressions: a module block whose source is not a literal is not resolved.

83.title: What it does not do

9.body: Every network fetch happens when the extension evaluates or a repository is fetched; build actions are offline, and what the engine sees at run time is a complete module directory. A terraform_module is one directory: srcs are the files the engine loads (.tf and .tf.json, plus .tofu and .tofu.json for tofu_module), all directly in the target's package, and anything else is an analysis error rather than a file the engine would silently skip. A nested directory of .tf files is a child module with its own target.
